syllabusTopics: Metals and metallurgical principles: definition of metallurgy and its types (hydrometallurgy, pyrometallurgy, electrometallurgy)
Introduction of ores; gangue or matrix, flux and slag, alloy and amalgam
General principles of extraction of metals: concentration, calcination and roasting, smelting, carbon reduction, thermite and electrochemical reduction
Alkali metals: general characteristics of alkali metals
Sodium: extraction from Down's process, properties (action with oxygen, water, acids, nonmetals and ammonia) and uses
Sodium hydroxide: properties (precipitation reaction and action with carbon monoxide) and uses
Sodium carbonate: properties (action with CO2, SO2, water, precipitation reactions) and uses
Alkaline earth metals: general characteristics of alkaline earth metals
Molecular formula and uses of quick lime, bleaching powder, magnesia, plaster of paris and epsom salt
Solubility of hydroxides, carbonates and sulphates of alkaline earth metals (general trend with explanation)
Stability of carbonate and nitrate of alkaline earth metals (general trend with explanation)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Metallurgy** is the science of winning a metal from its ore and refining it; its three branches map onto the activity series. **Hydrometallurgy** uses aqueous chemistry — gold is dissolved by cyanide leaching (2Au + 4CN⁻ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + 4OH⁻) and knocked out of solution by zinc.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - 2Au + 4CN⁻ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + 4OH⁻ (leaching) - 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → 2Au + [Zn(CN)₄]²⁻ (displacement) - Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂ (pyrometallurgy) - 2NaCl(l) —electrolysis→ 2Na + Cl₂ (electrometallurgy)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All atoms are identical in an element. ✅ Isotopes have same protons but different neutrons.  ·  ❌ Atoms are indivisible. ✅ Atoms consist of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Gold on a zinc shovel*** — cyanide leaching dissolves gold as [Au(CN)₂]⁻ even from ore worth grams per tonne; stirring with zinc shavings precipitates the gold: 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → 2Au + [Zn(CN)₄]²⁻ — hydrometallurgy turning tonnes of rock into a button of metal.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Three routes by height in the activity series: top -> electrolysis, middle -> coke, bottom -> leaching/native. One equation per route: Au+CN-, Fe2O3+CO, NaCl(l) electrolysis. Ore = profitable mineral.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): What is metallurgy? Name its three types with one example of each.** — **Metallurgy** is the science of extracting metals from their ores and preparing the pure metal for use; it covers concentration of the ore, conversion to a reducible compound, reduction and refining.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Why is aluminium extracted by electrolysis although aluminium is a strong reducing agent in the thermite reaction?** — In the thermite reaction aluminium takes oxygen from iron(III) oxide, 2Al + Fe₂O₃ → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe, showing Al has greater affinity for oxygen than iron.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: When asked to "name the types of metallurgy", give all three with one concrete example equation each — a bare list of names usually scores half.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The activity series is really a ΔG ladder: the more negative the oxide's free energy of formation, the harder carbon must fight to take the oxygen away — electrometallurgy is simply paying for the reversal with electrons instead of coke.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Metallurgy = extracting + refining metals from ores. Three types: hydrometallurgy (aqueous; Au cyanide leaching 2Au + 4CN- + O2 + 2H2O -> 2[Au(CN)2]- + 4OH-, displacement with Zn), pyrometallurgy (heat/coke; blast furnace Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2), electrometallurgy (electrolysis of molten salts; Downs Na,…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: About 90% of the world's gold was leached with cyanide solutions; a heap-leach pad can extract a gram of gold from a tonne of ore and still turn a profit.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Where Metals Come From Only a handful of metals — gold, platinum, some copper and silver — occur native. Everything else sits in the crust as **ores**: ionic compounds (oxides, sulphides, carbonates, chlorides) from which the metal must be won.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Metallurgy and its types - **Metallurgy** = the science and technology of extracting metals from their ores and preparing them for use. - **Hydrometallurgy** — extraction through aqueous solution chemistry: leaching the ore with a solvent (acid, cyanide), then precipitating or displacing the metal.…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.  ·  ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).  ·  ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.  ·  ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.  ·  ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).  ·  ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.
